turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Morning, Mrs Pillay. Quick one today, blood pressure and the cholesterol.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, doctor. I'm just here for the check, really. I don't know if I've got much to tell you.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She's got plenty. She's been very tired, her sleep is all over the place, and she stopped the cholesterol tablet.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag, I'm not that tired. I don't know, doctor. The sleep, ja, that's a bit true. And the tablet, well, actually, ja, I did stop it.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Which tablet?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): The cholesterol one. Atorvastatin.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Dose?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Twenty milligrams, at night. I stopped it in February. No, shame, March. I read something online.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Read what?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): About the muscles. People saying it eats your muscles or something. I got a fright. I don't know, doctor, maybe I shouldn't have.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any muscle pain now?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Not really. I don't think so.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Blood pressure tablet, still taking it?
[SEG0014] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ja, amlodipine, the ten milligram, every morning. She doesn't miss.
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No, he always does this. It's five, I think, and I only take it every other day. I don't know, doctor, the box is at home.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): It's once a day on the script. Any chest pain?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ankles swelling?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing like that.
[SEG0020] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She is short of breath, though. To the shop and back.
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): I am not. I don't know why he says that. On the hill I'm a bit puffed, but I'm not short of breath.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): Cough?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Headaches?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Um, well, actually once last week, but it went away. I don't know if that even counts.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long has the sleep been off?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. A while. He'll say weeks. I can't put a date on it.
[SEG0028] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): About three weeks. And she's been tired that whole time, proper tired.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): The tiredness I don't really agree with. A little, maybe, in the afternoons. Not the whole time.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sit. Blood pressure is 152 over 94. Pulse 76.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Heart sounds normal. Chest clear. No swelling at the ankles.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Is 152 bad? I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): A bit high. I suspect the every-other-day dosing. Not a crisis.
[SEG0034] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): If you're worried about sugar I can give her my metformin. Five hundred. I take it for diabetes.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): I never took your pills, and I'm not starting. Those are his, for his diabetes. I don't have sugar, doctor.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): Don't take his metformin. Did you start the aspirin I suggested last time?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I never took it. The chemist said something and I just left it on the shelf. I don't know.
[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke?
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Never.
[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): Alcohol?
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): A glass of wine at Christmas. Hardly ever. I don't know if that counts.
[SEG0042] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She smoked before we got married. Years back.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): That was one cigarette at a party. I don't count that. I never really smoked.
[SEG0044] person_1 (DOCTOR): We'll call it never. Any operations?
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long have you had the blood pressure?
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. Maybe ten years. I'm not sure of the year.
[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): Cholesterol problem is still on your record. Ongoing.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja. That's why I feel bad about the tablet. My daughter sent a link, some website from overseas, and I got scared.
[SEG0050] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Traffic was hectic coming in, hey. Load shedding, and the robot by the mall was out. We sat there forever.
[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll send you for bloods. Cholesterol, liver tests, and kidney function.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): Must I come starving? I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes, fasting. And take the amlodipine every day from tonight, not every second day.
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. I'll try. And the cholesterol one?
[SEG0055] person_1 (DOCTOR): We revisit that in a month, when the bloods are back. No lecture. You read something, you stopped, we decide then.
[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): Shame, thank you. I was waiting to be told off. The grandkids are with us this weekend, so I'll get a lift if the bloods are early.
[SEG0057] person_1 (DOCTOR): Book the bloods at the desk on your way out, and a review visit in a month. That's us.

spec.situation: Patient on routine review who admits stopping the cholesterol tablet after reading something online, still takes the BP tablet but 'every other day'; mentions husband's diabetes pills; doctor does not scold, plans repeat blood tests and revisits the statin decision in a month.
features: relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.

bad.reason: Transcript mentions husband's diabetes, not family history.

omissions.text: Atorvastatin was stopped in March (patient first said February, then corrected to March).
Patient stopped atorvastatin because she read online that it could 'eat your muscles' and got scared; daughter had sent the link.
Amlodipine dose is recorded without the unresolved dose discrepancy: family member said 10 mg every morning, patient said she thinks it is 5 mg and is not sure because the box is at home.
Doctor stated the amlodipine prescription is once daily on the script.
Patient denied diabetes ('I don't have sugar').
Patient never started aspirin that the doctor had suggested previously.
Patient declined taking husband’s metformin and stated she had never taken his pills.
Negative finding asked and answered: no headaches apart from one headache last week that resolved; the general denial of headaches is not separately recorded as a negative finding.
Doctor said the blood pressure was 'not a crisis.'
Plan was to revisit/reconsider the cholesterol tablet in a month when blood results are back, rather than restart immediately.
